query_raw: Should I tilt my head back when I have a nosebleed?
query_normalized: Should I tilt my head back when I have a nosebleed?

generation_raw.text:
No, you should not tilt your head back. According to NHS guidelines, if you have a nosebleed, you should sit down and lean forward, with your head tilted forward and your mouth open [1].

Tilting your head back can cause blood to run down the back of your throat, which may lead to swallowing a large amount of blood and vomiting [2]. Instead, while leaning forward, you should pinch your nose just above your nostrils for 10 to 15 minutes to help stop the bleeding [1].

*Disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only. If your nosebleed lasts longer than 10 to 15 minutes, seems excessive, or is accompanied by dizziness or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention [2]. Always consult a registered doctor for clinical diagnosis and advice.*
